about:
A PROJECT-DEFINED EDITORIAL EQUIVALENT, NOT AN EXTERNAL SYLLABUS. NOTHING IN THIS FILE MAY BE ATTRIBUTED TO ANY MALAYALAM EXAMINING OR LANGUAGE BODY. core/exam-levels.json records malayalam as exam 'no widely-sat ladder', basis 'editorial', and it carries NO caveat -- so unlike Tamil, whose entry names its diglossia, this track hands the inventory no external steer at all. Kerala's state school syllabi and the Kerala Sahitya Akademi exist, but they are built for children schooled in Malayalam or for literary attainment rather than for an adult second-language learner against CEFR can-do descriptors, and neither was consulted. Read 'A1' here as the CEFR descriptor -- can greet, introduce oneself, and handle a short exchange in everyday spoken Malayalam -- and as a measuring stick this project built for itself.

EXAM ENVELOPE: NONE EXISTS. There is no malayalam/task-shapes/ and no malayalam/mocks/, and no malayalam/assessment.json. So unlike Hindi and Marathi, whose inventories could mine a checked-in mock for the exponent a paper item actually needs, nothing here can say which task demands which word. Where those files write 'the mock asks for X', this one can only write 'an A1 learner needs X'. That is a weaker claim and is stated as one.

SEARCH FOR AN EXTERNAL SOURCE: NOT SEARCHED, BY INSTRUCTION. The project settled at HL-C287/HL-C290 that the proxy derivation is the method for tracks with no sat ladder, and the search was deliberately not redone for Malayalam. Saying so is what keeps 'we did not look' from reading as 'there is nothing to find'.

THE REGISTER COLUMN IS MEASURED, NOT BORROWED. Tamil's inventory carries a register column because core/exam-levels.json names Tamil's diglossia in a caveat. Malayalam has no caveat, so this file measured the corpus instead of importing Tamil's shape. What it found is a DIFFERENT axis: four lessons carry register 'formal' and every one is a Sanskrit-tatsama time-of-day greeting, two carry 'literary'/'literary-narrative' and both teach a native word the everyday Sanskrit one displaced, and one teaches respect as grammatical plurality. That is a lexical borrowed-against-inherited split plus an honorific, and this file claims exactly that and does not claim a literary/spoken diglossia. The eighteen lessons carrying variety 'standard' rather than 'standard-colloquial' were checked and are ALL writing lessons, so they are an artefact of the script runway and not evidence of a second variety.
source: PROJECT-DEFINED. LEVEL PROXY: code/learning/human-languages/core/exam-inventory-es-a1.json, the DELE/PCIC-sourced Spanish A1 point set, used for the STRUCTURE of what an A1 learner must handle. Its own source is the Instituto Cervantes Plan Curricular inventories. The proxy supplies the LEVEL and the shape of the columns; every Malayalam exponent is this project's choice, and every point records which Spanish point or points it was derived from.

anchors.title: code/learning/human-languages/core/exam-inventory-es-a1.json
anchors.note: The DELE/PCIC-sourced Spanish A1 point set, used for the STRUCTURE of what an A1 learner must handle. Spanish is a proxy for LEVEL, never for grammar: each point was read as 'what must an A1 learner be able to do here', and the Malayalam exponent that carries the same load was then chosen. Where Malayalam carries the load with machinery Spanish does not have -- case suffixes, a dative subject, a question particle, a verb that never agrees -- the point is restated around the Malayalam machinery and its Spanish origin recorded in derivedFrom.

anchors.title: Council of Europe, CEFR Companion Volume
anchors.note: Supplies the meaning of 'A1' as a can-do band. It describes what a learner can DO and names no language's forms, which is exactly why a second, language-shaped source was needed and why the Spanish inventory is used as the proxy for that shape.

anchors.title: malayalam/lessons/ as merged on main
anchors.note: 292 lessons, all schema_version 2, introducing 358 atoms. Every probe in this file names an atom drawn from this set and was checked mechanically against it before the file was written; no probe names an id that a future lesson is expected to introduce.

anchors.title: this project's judgement about Malayalam
anchors.note: Where a Spanish point has no single Malayalam exponent, the choice of which Malayalam form carries the load is this project's and is defended in the point's own note. The clearest cases are the dative subject standing in for gustar, undu standing in for both hay and tener, and the -o particle standing in for Spanish interrogative inversion.

communicative-functions.source: Derived from the PCIC functional inventory by way of core/exam-inventory-es-a1.json.
communicative-functions.note: The Spanish functional subsections were walked in full and each was answered with the Malayalam exponent that carries it. Partial because the answers are this project's editorial choices rather than an examining body's list, and because no Malayalam mock exists to check them against.

grammar.source: Derived from the PCIC grammar inventory by way of core/exam-inventory-es-a1.json.
grammar.note: Every Spanish A1 grammar category was answered, including the ones whose Malayalam answer is that the category does not exist. Partial because a Malayalam-shaped grammar inventory would enumerate categories Spanish never raises -- the full case series, the relative participle, the quotative -- and this file reaches those only where a Spanish point happened to point at them.

phonology-orthography.source: Derived from the PCIC orthography inventory, plus this track's own script lessons.
phonology-orthography.note: The script column is measured against the corpus rather than against Malayalam: 67 distinct characters appear in headwords and 58 are taught. Partial for two reasons -- the nine untaught characters, and the fact that the pronunciation points are answered by SHAPE lessons rather than by sound lessons, which is honest and thin.

lexicon.source: Derived from the PCIC notional inventories by way of core/exam-inventory-es-a1.json.
lexicon.note: All twenty Spanish specific-notion areas were walked. Seven of them -- leisure, media, money and shopping, services, medicine, the arts, technology -- have no Malayalam word in the corpus at all, and are enumerated as uncovered rather than omitted.

probeSemantics: A probe is the set of atoms whose presence in the corpus demonstrates the point. ALL of them must be introduced for the point to count: a point covered by half its atoms is not covered, because a candidate asked for the whole of something does not get partial credit for half of it. probe: null means nothing in the corpus corresponds to the point, and every null carries a note naming what is missing -- those notes are a work queue and are written as one.
